title: Why every cancer is different
blurb: Different mutations and different cell types mean different weak spots.

text.simple: Two people can both have 'lung cancer', but the broken genes inside their tumors can be completely different.
text.student: Sequencing thousands of tumors shows each has its own mix of driver mutations, even within the same organ. [@vogelstein2013] [@pcawg2020]
text.deep: Pan-cancer whole-genome analyses find on average 4–5 driver mutations per tumor, with substantial inter- and intra-tumor heterogeneity. [@pcawg2020]

steps.title: Where the cell came from matters

text.simple: A blood cell and an eye cell use different genes every day. So the same broken gene can have different effects in each.
text.student: Cell type ('lineage') shapes which genes are active and which ones a cell depends on.
text.deep: Lineage determines chromatin state, expressed genes and dependencies; driver effects are strongly context-dependent. [@vogelstein2013]

steps.title: Try it: same knockdown, two cells

note.simple: Turning off CDK6 slows the division program in the blood cancer cell, but barely touches the eye cell. Blood cells lean on CDK6 more.
note.student: ● Measured in both: CDK6 knockdown lowers K562's division program, with almost no change in RPE1. The drug palbociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6.
note.deep: Hematopoietic cells rely more on CDK6 (and cyclin D3, try CCND3), whereas epithelial cells rely more on CDK4/cyclin D1, an example of lineage-specific dependency.

text.simple: Because every cancer is different, doctors now often test a tumor's genes to choose a treatment. But that's for doctors to decide, not this app!
text.student: This is the idea behind **precision oncology**: match treatment to a tumor's specific changes. [@nci_targeted] This app is a learning tool and can't make that match for anyone.
text.deep: Biomarker-driven therapy (e.g., BCR-ABL1 → imatinib, KRAS G12C → sotorasib) depends on validated companion diagnostics and clinical evidence, not cell-line data alone. [@nci_targeted]
